newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BT Fund sees shifts in HK blue chip shareholders.
newsitem.headline: BT Fund sees shifts in HK blue chip shareholders.

text.p: Increased mainland Chinese interest in taking stakes in major Hong Kong blue chips after the territory returns to China on July 1 is likely to underpin the strong performance of the Hong Kong stock market, BT Fund Managers Ltd said.
"I think this will be a real phenomenon," vice president Dio Wong told a news conference on Monday.
While Hongkong Telecom was likely to complete a link-up with a Chinese partner, Wong said the HSBC group could also see some Chinese interest, possibly involving its Hang Seng Bank Ltd unit.
"Hang Seng Bank is a very strong bank - there is so much excess capital. I think the Chinese look at Hang Seng Bank and think this is great," he said.
Wong also saw a consolidation in the utilities industry, involving China Light & Power Co Ltd and Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd.

"There will be a change probably in the structure of the utilities. It makes no sense now for there to be two utilities in Hong Kong," he said. "There may be some sort of merger, there might be a Chinese shareholder."

BT Fund Managers said on Monday it expects the Hang Seng Index to reach 15,500 points by year-end with a possibility that the blue chip index could overshoot and reach 16,000 or more. It closed on Monday at 14,574.64.
"Corporate factors related to the handover period and the handover itself ensure that the market will tend to look towards the upside," said Wong.
